newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banco de Mexico net reserves, assets rise.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Mexico net reserves, assets rise.

text.p: Banco de Mexico said on Tuesday its international reserves as of May 23 were $22.181 billion, compared to $21.727 billion on May 16.
The central bank said that its net international assets as of the same date rose to $13.533 billion from $12.910 billion the week before.
The central bank said the increase of $623 million in net international assets during the period was due to:
--The purchase of $300 million from credit institutions, the product of the exercising of options on the sale of dollars to the central bank that were issued during the auction of April 30.
--Net income from operations by the state oil company Pemex worth $229 million.
--Net purchases of foreign currency from the federal government worth $45 million.

--A net gain of $49 million for a combination of factors including changes in the dollar value of non-dollar assets and liabilities held by the bank; net returns on interest rates and from trading of metals and securities; and net deposits in dollar accounts from commercial banks at the central bank.
Banco de Mexico said that between May 16 and May 23 the monetary base fell 3.206 billion pesos due to a fall in the seasonal demand of bills and coins.

In the same period, the government's balance at the central bank rose 7.662 billion pesos, due to tax collection. At the same time, the deposits of the federal government's bank bailout program Fobaproa in the central bank fell by 1.193 billion pesos.

The bank said it sold government securities worth 530 million pesos in order to neutralize the added liquidity from the increase in reserves, the lower amount of Fobaproa deposits and the contraction in the monetary base.
The following tables detail Banco de Mexico's reserves and net domestic credit. All figures are in billions of pesos, unless otherwise indicated.
May 16 May 23
International Reserves
U.S. Dollars $21.727 bln $22.181 bln
Monetary Base 80.135 76.929
Net International Assets*
U.S. Dollars $12.910 bln $13.533 bln
Net Domestic Credit -21.778 -29.616
*Net International Assets are defined as gross international assets minus central bank liabilities with the IMF and assets of less than a six-month duration from other central banks.
((--David Luhnow, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-7902))
